# Leaftext — full page index

> Refine your mind. Your thoughts, secure and free. A free desktop app for reading and writing your own documents, on your own machine. Every canonical page, its human URL, its raw Markdown source, and a short description. Fetch the .md URLs for clean, JS-free text.

## Refine your mind.
- Page: https://leaftext.com/
- Markdown: https://leaftext.com/README.md
- Summary: Run your agents as a team, talk to a bot of your own, and read every file — all on your machine.

## Rendering
- Page: https://leaftext.com/docs/01-features/01-rendering.html
- Markdown: https://leaftext.com/docs/01-features/01-rendering.md
- Summary: Open a file and Leaftext draws it as a clean page in your theme. Markdown reads the way GitHub draws it, and data files, email, Office documents and books get pages of their own.

## Navigation
- Page: https://leaftext.com/docs/01-features/02-navigation.html
- Markdown: https://leaftext.com/docs/01-features/02-navigation.md
- Summary: Keep many documents open, move back and forth between them, and find your way around a long one. Leaftext remembers where you were in every tab.

## Library
- Page: https://leaftext.com/docs/01-features/03-library.html
- Markdown: https://leaftext.com/docs/01-features/03-library.md
- Summary: Point Leaftext at a folder, and it becomes a vault: a file tree to browse, text to search, and a map of how its documents link. Opening a vault adds no files to your folder.

## Minimap
- Page: https://leaftext.com/docs/01-features/04-minimap.html
- Markdown: https://leaftext.com/docs/01-features/04-minimap.md
- Summary: A tiny copy of your document runs down the right edge, real text rather than bars, with a box showing what is on screen. Click to jump, drag the box to scroll, or turn the wheel over it.

## Settings
- Page: https://leaftext.com/docs/01-features/05-settings.html
- Markdown: https://leaftext.com/docs/01-features/05-settings.md
- Summary: There is no settings panel. Each control stands where it applies, and every choice is kept in a plain file on your computer that you can read.

## Themes
- Page: https://leaftext.com/docs/01-features/06-themes.html
- Markdown: https://leaftext.com/docs/01-features/06-themes.md
- Summary: Every theme changes the whole window: the page, the controls, code, diagrams and the minimap. Each family carries its own fonts, so it reads as a different book, not just a different color.

## Editing
- Page: https://leaftext.com/docs/01-features/07-editing.html
- Markdown: https://leaftext.com/docs/01-features/07-editing.md
- Summary: Click into a sentence and type, and your change is written back into the file at that exact spot. When you would rather see the raw text, the code view shows the file's source. Both write to the sa...

## Relational tables
- Page: https://leaftext.com/docs/01-features/08-relational-tables.html
- Markdown: https://leaftext.com/docs/01-features/08-relational-tables.md
- Summary: Put each row's name in the first column, and Leaftext can show the table as records. Lay it out as cards, sort and filter it, and link rows across notes. The table stays plain Markdown, so it opens...

## Your Grove
- Page: https://leaftext.com/docs/01-features/09-progress.html
- Markdown: https://leaftext.com/docs/01-features/09-progress.md
- Summary: Leaftext keeps a quiet record of what you do and shows it as your Grove. Reading, writing, searching and the rest each grow their own area, and everything fills one Grove level. Each level brings s...

## Your own AI agent in Leaftext
- Page: https://leaftext.com/docs/01-features/10-agents.html
- Markdown: https://leaftext.com/docs/01-features/10-agents.md
- Summary: Each agent runs in a console next to the page you are reading. It uses your own account and model, sees what you see, and can read, edit and check the open document with you.

## Meet Leaftext
- Page: https://leaftext.com/docs/01-introduction.html
- Markdown: https://leaftext.com/docs/01-introduction.md
- Summary: Leaftext is a free app for Windows and macOS. It runs your AI agents as a team, gives you a bot of your own, and turns the files you already have into pages worth reading.

## Installation
- Page: https://leaftext.com/docs/02-installation.html
- Markdown: https://leaftext.com/docs/02-installation.md
- Summary: Leaftext is free. There is no account to create and nothing else to install first. The first time you open it, macOS or Windows warns you once, and the steps below clear that in a few clicks.

## Quickstart
- Page: https://leaftext.com/docs/03-quickstart.html
- Markdown: https://leaftext.com/docs/03-quickstart.md
- Summary: There is nothing to set up: no account, no folder to choose, no plugins. Open a file you already have and start reading.

## Get help
- Page: https://leaftext.com/docs/04-help.html
- Markdown: https://leaftext.com/docs/04-help.md
- Summary: Leaftext is made by one person, so there is no support desk. Questions are asked and answered in public, so the answer you get is the one the next person finds.

## How it compares
- Page: https://leaftext.com/docs/05-compare.html
- Markdown: https://leaftext.com/docs/05-compare.md
- Summary: Each of these apps is good at something. Obsidian links Markdown notes and has a large plugin library. Typora writes Markdown in the finished page. Calibre manages and reads a library of ebooks.

## Privacy
- Page: https://leaftext.com/docs/07-privacy.html
- Markdown: https://leaftext.com/docs/07-privacy.md
- Summary: Leaftext has no account and no server. Nothing you open, write or connect is ever sent to the maker of the app.
